notesStmt.note: A note on the verso, in Whitman's hand, gives a date of "Dec '88," but in a letter to Richard Maurice Bucke, dated November 10, 1888, Whitman writes that he has "finished the little beginning & end Notes I spoke of for the big book and sent to the printer." It therefore seems that this manuscript was written sometime in early November of 1888.

A manuscript draft of "Note at Beginning," which appeared between the title page and the table of contents of Whitman's Complete Poems & Prose (1888–9). On the other side of the sheet is a deleted manuscript section from the same volume's "Note at End of Complete Poems and Prose."

body.p: ¶ (When I had started got this Vol. well under way, I was ‸quite suddenly prostrated by illness ‸paralysis‸— continued yet——which will have to excuse many faults both of omission and commission in it.)

¶ But I will would not let the great and momentous era of these years, these States, slip away without attempting to arrest in a special printed Book (as much in spirit as letter and may䦘be for the future more than the present) some few specimens— —even vital throbs, breaths—as representations of it all from my point of view, and right from the midst of it, and at the time.

¶ There is a tally ‸and, stamp and stage ⹀result of periods and Nations, elusive, at second or third hand, mostly often escaping the historian of matter⹀of⹀fact—in some sort that the Nation's spiritual ‸formative ferment or chaos—the getting in of its essence, and shape formulating identity—a law of it, and most significant part of its progress. (Of the best of events and facts, even the most important, there are finally not the events and facts only, but something flashing out and fluctuating like tuft⹀flames or eidólons, from all.) My going up and down amidst these years, and the impromptu jottings of their sights and thoughts, of war and peace, have been in accordance of with that law, and probably a result of it . . . . In certain respects, (emotionality, passions, spirituality, the invisible trend,) I therefore launch ‸forth) the ‸divisions of the following Book forth as not only a genuine consequent of that period and its influences, but even in a one sort as a History of America, the past 35 years, after the rest and after the adjuncts of that History, have been studied and attended to.
